comment: The classification of every difference the Storage compat run finds (summarize.mjs for the suites, captures.mjs for the captures). Classes: a, a bug in Aruma (fixed, with a test, or listed); b, a difference ADR-023 §3 lists (item is its number); c, a bug in the emulator, with the evidence that production differs. A capture rule names one kind of difference: its key and values are patterns, * any run of characters, and the first rule that matches classifies it, so the rules about one step come before the general ones.

ct | Firebase Storage JavaScript SDK con.note: an object stored over GCS without Content-Disposition downloads with attachment; filename*=utf-8''testFile; the test wants filename*=testFile, without the charset RFC 8187 requires

ct | GCS endpoint conformance tests Head.note: the same default Content-Disposition, on the GCS download

ct | Firebase Storage endpoint conforman.note: supertest's .send({}) makes the finalize carry the two bytes {} without X-Goog-Upload-Offset; a finalize alone must have an empty body (400)
Authorization: Bearer somethingElse is a credential that is not accepted: 401, as in RTDB; the test wants 403

ct | GCS Javascript SDK conformance test.note: one bucket per project: the test's other-bucket does not exist, 404 The specified bucket does not exist.
makePublic patches the object's ACL: 501 notImplemented
the same makePublic, before a read through the XML API path

the object resource has timeFinalized, as GCS's own API description does (google.golang.org/api storage/v1 Object.TimeFinalized, which cloud.google.com/go/storage 1.62.1 reads as ObjectAttrs.Finalized); the test's exact key list, the emulator's, lacks it
the same timeFinalized, in the exact key list of a PATCH's reply
emulatorOnly, outside the count: a rewriteToken sent is 400 here, 501 in the emulator

ct | GCS endpoint conformance tests Uplo.note: emulatorOnly, outside the count: POST policy uploads are the XML API, which v0.3 does not serve (ADR-023 §2)

captures.note: a pageToken is opaque and signed, bound to the listing (ADR-022 §13); the emulator's is the last name
JSON replies say charset=UTF-8, as production does (production/bucket_probe.json); the emulator writes utf-8
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every /v0 reply, Origin or not, as production does on its error replies (bucket_probe.json); the emulator only answers an Origin
Cache-Control: private, max-age=0 on /v0 JSON, as production (bucket_probe.json, E §1); the emulator sends none
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate on GCS JSON, as production (bucket_probe.json, ADR-023 §3-79); the emulator sends none
empty custom metadata left out of a /v0 resource; the emulator writes "metadata": {}

timeFinalized in a GCS object resource: GCS's own API description has it (google.golang.org/api storage/v1 TimeFinalized, read by cloud.google.com/go/storage 1.62.1 as Finalized); the emulator leaves it out
the stored default contentDisposition is inline; filename*=utf-8''<name>, as a deployed bucket stores it (PY-RR); the emulator stores inline
a download carries the stored inline; filename*=utf-8''<name> (PY-RR); the emulator writes filename*=<name> without the charset RFC 8187 requires
a download with no stored Content-Disposition is attachment; filename*=utf-8''<name>; the emulator writes filename*=<name> without the charset

no Content-Encoding on an identity download; the emulator sends an empty one, which names no content coding (RFC 9110 §8.4), where GCS marks such an object with x-goog-stored-content-encoding: identity (below)

x-goog-stored-content-encoding on every download, as GCS sends it: @google-cloud/storage reads it to decide whether to check the hashes (file.js safeToValidate), Go's reader to tell server decompression (B §6.3); the emulator sends none
a download with no stored Cache-Control is private, max-age=0 (token link; a rules-decided one is private too, §3-42 and §3-90); the emulator sends an empty one
the emulator copies an object's stored Cache-Control onto the JSON reply about it (a PATCH's); a JSON reply is not the object, and production's JSON replies are private, max-age=0 (bucket_probe.json)
the emulator copies an object's Content-Disposition onto JSON replies about it (PATCH, admin reads); production's JSON replies carry none (bucket_probe.json)
the 403 text is Permission denied.; the emulator names the permission; no SDK reads it (A §5.1)
Go's readers, without WithJSONReads, read through the XML API path (/<bucket>/<object>), which Aruma does not serve: Go needs WithJSONReads (adminstorage)

captures.key: admin_go | Writer small, default ChunkSize (16 MiB) | x0.field.contentType
captures.note: a multipart upload whose JSON part has no contentType takes the media part's (the type Go sniffs), as GCS documents for multipart uploads and B §5.2 reads from the SDKs; the emulator ignores the media part's type

captures.key: admin_gcs_endpoint | file.save 9 MiB chunkSize 4 MiB (resumable, chunked) | *
captures.note: the GCS resumable protocol whole: Node's chunks get 308 with Range and the upload ends whole; the emulator ends a session on its first chunk (B §9), so Node's chunked save fails

captures.key: admin_go | Writer 9 MiB, ChunkSize 4 MiB (resumable, 3 chunks) | *
captures.note: the same for Go: its chunks get 200 with X-Http-Status-Code-Override: 308 and the upload ends whole; the emulator ends the session on the first chunk and Go fails on its OK body
a GCS resumable start has no body, as GCS documents it (a 200 with Location); the emulator's says OK in text/plain
the same bodiless start for a one-request resumable save
objects.patch over GCS is served; the emulator answers 501 Not Implemented to Go's Update
objects.patch under /storage/v1 with useAuthWithCustomEndpoint is served; the emulator answers 501
rewriteTo is served; the emulator answers Go's CopierFrom 501
ifGenerationMatch=0 on an existing object is 412 conditionNotMet; the emulator ignores the precondition and overwrites
the same 412 for Node's save with ifGenerationMatch=0; the emulator overwrites
buckets.get answers for the project's bucket, so bucket.exists() is true; the emulator answers 404
the same buckets.get for bucket.getMetadata()
the same buckets.get for Go's Bucket.Attrs
follows from the emulator's failures above: big.bin and copy.txt exist here (the resumable upload and the copy worked), so their deletes are 204
follows from the emulator's failed resumable uploads: big.bin is in the listing here
the same big.bin, deleted at the cleanup
a pageToken that is not one is 400; the emulator lists from it

captures.key: sdk_list | raw list prefix without trailing slash | *
captures.note: a list prefix without a trailing / is served, decided on its folder; the emulator refuses it 400

maxResults counts items and prefixes together and a page holds them in name order (GCS objects.list: "Maximum combined number of entries in items[] and prefixes[]"), so a third page holds what was left; the emulator returns every prefix on every page

captures.key: sdk_read | GET metadata with Bearer instead of Firebase | *
captures.note: Bearer <ID token> on /v0 is a credential that is not accepted: 401; the emulator takes it
Firebase not-a-token is a credential that is not accepted: 401; the emulator ignores it and lets the rules deny, 403
an unsigned ID token is refused, 401: production checks the signature (E §7); the emulator believes it

captures.key: rules | token on the metadata URL (no alt=media), no auth | *
captures.note: a download token opens the bytes, not the metadata; the emulator opens both
a client cannot plant a download token by PATCH (E §5); the emulator adds mine-1 to the tokens
so the planted token opens nothing, 403; it opens the object in the emulator
create_token and delete_token without the admin's credential are 403 Permission denied.; the emulator says Missing admin credentials.
a chunk at an offset past the size received is 400 with the size; the emulator ignores offsets and appends
follows: the emulator appended the gap's and the overlap's bytes too, so its sizes are 10 more
the same: the object is the 20 bytes sent in order, the emulator's 30 with the misplaced ones
a finalize short of the size announced at start is 400 with final, no object; the emulator stores the 4 bytes
a finalize that brings no byte past the end of a finished session is a repeat: 200 with final and the saved metadata; the emulator answers 400
a byte past the end of a finished session is 400 with final and the size; the emulator's 400 has no status
a query on a finished session answers with the object's metadata; the emulator with OK
cancel answers X-Goog-Upload-Status: cancelled (E §3.1); the emulator sends no status
a chunk or finalize on a cancelled session is 400 with final; the emulator's 400 has no status

captures.key: raw_upload | multipart by hand, name in metadata only | *
captures.note: a multipart upload named in metadata.name alone is taken; the emulator refuses it 400

an unknown bucket is 404 Not Found. as production answers (bucket_probe.json, where a multipart upload's 404 has no X-Goog-Upload-Status); the emulator creates the bucket and lets the rules deny, 403 with final
a body whose boundary is not the Content-Type's is 400 with a JSON body, as production's errors are (bucket_probe.json); the emulator's is a text body
the API's CORS is *, whatever the Origin, as production's (bucket_probe.json, sent with an Origin); the emulator echoes the Origin
a PATCH body that is not JSON is 400 with a JSON error, as production's errors are (bucket_probe.json); the emulator answers an HTML stack trace
the objects left at the end follow from two outcomes above: open/raw/short.txt is not stored here (§3-23, the short finalize), and open/rawup/mp.txt is (§3-26, named in its metadata alone)
a one-request upload (multipart) denied by the rules is 403 without X-Goog-Upload-Status, as production's multipart replies carry none (bucket_probe.json); the emulator adds final
the /v0 resumable start, chunk, query and cancel replies have no body; the emulator's say OK in text/plain
every chunk and finalize reply carries X-Goog-Upload-Size-Received, not only a query's; the emulator sends it on query alone
errors are JSON {"error":{"code","message"}}, as production's (bucket_probe.json, E §1); the emulator answers some with plain text
a missing object is 404 with production's JSON body (bucket_probe.json); the emulator's is the text Not Found
a 400 has a JSON body as production's errors do (bucket_probe.json); the emulator's is the text Bad Request
